title: Letter sounds s-a-t-p-i-n
keywords: s a t p i n
examples: Teacher, what sound does the letter 's' make?
Can you show me how to make the sound for 'a'?
Where is the letter 't' on the chart?

explain.say: Each letter makes a sound. You say the sound short and clear.

draw.text: s a t p i n

explain.say: The letter s makes the first sound in sun. It is a long, quiet sound.
The letter a makes the first sound in apple. Open your mouth wide.
The letter t makes the first sound in tap. Your tongue taps behind your top teeth.
The letter p makes the first sound in pen. Close your lips, then let a little air out.
The letter i makes the first sound in insect. The letter n makes the first sound in net.
Each letter has a name and a sound. Here you say the sound, with no extra uh at the end.

draw.text: Say the sound, not the name

faq.q: Why do I not say 'uh' when I say the sound for 'a'?
faq.a: The pure sound for 'a' is a short, quick sound. It is not the sound you make when you say 'uh'.
asks: What is the right sound for 'a'?
Should I add an extra sound to 'a'?

faq.q: How do I know if my mouth shape is correct for 's'?
faq.a: Try making the sound while looking in a mirror. Your mouth should look like a thin, straight line.
asks: What does my mouth look like for 's'?
Can you check my mouth shape for 's'?

faq.q: Is the sound for 't' the same as the sound for 'd'?
faq.a: Your tongue is in the same place for both. For d, your voice is on. For t, your voice is off. Put a hand on your throat to feel it.
asks: What is the difference between 't' and 'd' sounds?
How do I make the 't' sound?

faq.q: If I see the letter 'p', what sound should I make?
faq.a: You should make a short, popping sound. It is like blowing a little puff of air.
asks: Say the sound for this letter.

faq.q: Do I need to use my hands when I make the letter sounds?
faq.a: You only need your mouth to make the sounds. Some children like to add an action for each sound, and that is fine too.
asks: Do I move my body for phonics?
Is it okay to use my hands?

facts: Phonics teaches the relationship between letters and sounds.
Pure sounds are the short, clear sounds that each letter makes.
The letter 's' makes the sound at the start of sun.
The letter 'a' makes a short /a/ sound, like in apple.

quiz.say: Look at the letter. Tap the picture that starts with its sound.
quiz.why: Tiger starts with the sound of t. Your tongue taps behind your top teeth.

wrong.0: Duck starts with the sound of d, which uses your voice.
wrong.2: Sun starts with the sound of s, a long quiet sound.

quiz.say: Look at the letter. Tap the picture that starts with its sound.
quiz.why: Pig starts with the sound of p. Your lips close, then a little air comes out.

wrong.0: Bear starts with the sound of b, which uses your voice.
wrong.1: Net starts with the sound of n, which comes through your nose.

quiz.say: Look at the ant. Say its first sound. Tap the letter.
quiz.why: Ant starts with the sound of a, as in apple.

wrong.1: The letter i makes the first sound in insect.
wrong.2: The letter t makes the last sound in ant.
